segment.description: Buffalo Creek in Grainger County, Tennessee — the TWRA-stocked trout stream near Rutledge and Tampico that runs through Buffalo Springs WMA (TWRA's 342-acre WMA with the Buffalo Springs trout hatchery on site). Explicitly a different stream from Buffalo Creek at Norris in Anderson County (USGS 03534500), as the catalog notes.
segment.boundaries: TWRA regulation exceptions treat 'Buffalo Creek (and tributaries) within the WMA boundary, Grainger County' as one unit: from the mill dam upstream is closed year-round to all fishing; from the mill dam downstream is open year-round to rod-and-reel fishing. Temperature evidence cited here is from the TDEC monitoring point at the Tamipco Road bridge (36.1941,-83.5627), the same reach USGS lists as 'BUFFALO CREEK AT TAMPICO, TN' (USGS 03494530, HUC 06010104, Grainger County).

coldSource.notes: No dam on the stocked reach. TWRA's Buffalo Springs WMA page (Grainger County) places a fish hatchery on the WMA and describes Buffalo Creek itself as accessible along the WMA dirt road; the WMA sits ~1 km upstream of the Tampico gauge point, tying the stocked creek to the same watershed as the temperature record. The catchment is a ~19.6 sq mi lowland Grainger County basin (USGS 03494528 'BUFFALO CREEK NR TAMPICO' drainage area); no gorge, gradient, or canopy description found on an agency page.

holdover.detail: No site-specific holdover survey exists. The program structure itself documents multi-month carry-over of stocked fish: TWRA's exceptions text sets a Delayed Harvest season on Buffalo Creek (WMA boundary reach) from Oct 1 to Jan 31 with catch-and-release and artificial lures only, i.e., fall-stocked trout must survive in-stream for months to be available to the Feb 1-Sept 30 harvest season that follows.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout listing or natural-reproduction documentation found for Buffalo Creek (Grainger). The TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 treats wild trout as an East Tennessee mountain/tailwater phenomenon and lists hatchery-supported streams as warmwater habitats; Buffalo Creek appears only as a stocked stream, and all workbook stocking rows are hatchery rainbow trout. (Name collision note: TWRA's Buffalo Springs HATCHERY is on this WMA — 'Buffalo' there refers to the spring/hatchery, not a wild trout stream.)

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TDEC grab samples at the Tamipco Road bridge show summer water of only 15.5-19.2 C across 2010-2025 (12 Jun-Sep observations, max 19.16 C in Jul 2024), and TWRA stocks the creek weekly from February through August plus an Oct 1-Jan 31 delayed-harvest catch-and-release season — near-year-round trout presence both measured and programmatic.
